Here are the values for standard usage parameters—indoor setpoint, air change rate, internal gains, and domestic hot water demand—grounded directly in your uploaded sources.

---

### 1. Indoor Setpoint Temperature (\\(\theta_{\text{int}}\\) / \\(T_{\text{set}}\\))

* **20.0 °C** (Standard Normative Setpoint)
  * **Source Title**: *TABULA Common Calculation Method* (IWU / TABULA) [1, 2]
  * **Table / Section / Page**: Section 2.1, Table 1, Page 11 (also Appendix, Page 29) [2]
  * **Building Type**: Residential buildings (Single-unit housing & Multi-unit housing) [2]
  * **Year of Data**: 2013 [2]

* **20.0 °C** (Swiss Heating Baseline Target)
  * **Source Title**: *Field Experience with Residential Heat Pumps in Switzerland...* (14th IEA Heat Pump Conference 2023, Paper 478) [3, 4]
  * **Table / Section / Page**: Section 2 (System boundaries and key performance indicators), Page 3 & Nomenclature, Page 11 [3, 4]
  * **Building Type**: Residential buildings (New builds & Renovations) [3]
  * **Year of Data**: 2023 [5]

* **20.0 °C** (Swiss Degree-Day Base Setpoint)
  * **Source Title**: *2503.16993v1 (1).pdf* (HEAPO Preprint) [6]
  * **Table / Section / Page**: Section 2.1.3 ("Weather Data"), Page 3, Formula (1) [6]
  * **Building Type**: Single-family and Multi-family residential buildings [7]
  * **Year of Data**: 2025 (citing SIA 381/3:1982 standard) [6, 8]

---

### 2. Standard Air Change Rate (\\(n_{\text{air}}\\))

* **0.40 h⁻¹** (Utilization / Usage Air Change Rate, \\(n_{\text{air,use}}\\))
  * **Source Title**: *TABULA Common Calculation Method* (IWU / TABULA) [9, 10]
  * **Table / Section / Page**: Section 2.3, Table 1, Page 11 (also Appendix, Page 29) [9, 10]
  * **Building Type**: Residential buildings (Single-unit housing & Multi-unit housing) [2, 9]
  * **Year of Data**: 2013

* **0.20 h⁻¹** (Infiltration Air Change Rate, \\(n_{\text{air,infilt}}\\))
  * **Source Title**: *TABULA Common Calculation Method* (IWU / TABULA) [11]
  * **Table / Section / Page**: Appendix (Energy Balance Calculation Example), Page 48 (yielding a total combined air change rate of \\(n = n_{\text{use}} + n_{\text{infilt}} = 0.40 + 0.20 = 0.60\text{ h}^{-1}\\)) [11]
  * **Building Type**: Multi-unit housing (MFH example building) [11]
  * **Year of Data**: 2013 [11]

* **Minimum Air Change Rate under EN 12831**:
  * **Status**: **not in the sources** (The excerpt for *prEN 12831-1:2025* lists table of contents headings for "Air change rate" in Annex A.3.4, but does not contain the numerical values) [12, 13].

---

### 3. Internal Heat Gains (\\(\phi_{\text{int}}\\) / \\(q_{\text{int}}\\))

* **3.0 W/m²** (Average Internal Heat Sources per m² Reference Area)
  * **Source Title**: *TABULA Common Calculation Method* (IWU / TABULA) [9, 14]
  * **Table / Section / Page**: Section 2.1, Table 1, Page 11 (also Appendix, Page 48) [9, 14]
  * **Building Type**: Residential buildings (Single-unit housing & Multi-unit housing) [2, 9]
  * **Year of Data**: 2013 [2]

* **2.4 W/m²** (Alternative TABULA Default Internal Heat Output)
  * **Source Title**: *TABULA Common Calculation Method* (IWU / TABULA) [15]
  * **Table / Section / Page**: Section 8, Table 1 / Appendix, Page 29 [15]
  * **Building Type**: Residential buildings [2, 15]
  * **Year of Data**: 2013

* **33.3 kWh/m²a** (\\(\approx \mathbf{3.80\text{ W/m}^2}\\)) (Electrical Appliances / Internal Gains Baseline)
  * **Source Title**: *Erweiterung des Gebäudeparkmodells gemäss SIA-Effizienzpfad Energie* (TEP Energy) [16]
  * **Table / Section / Page**: Section 4.1 / Table Basisfall 2010, Page 158 [16]
  * **Building Type**: Single-family house (**EFH**) and Multi-family house (**MFH**) [16]
  * **Year of Data**: 2010 baseline [16]

---

### 4. Domestic Hot Water (DHW) Demand per Person

#### **A. Normative Planning Standards (SIA 385/2)**
* **Source Title**: *Task 1 - Test procedures and Quality Labels for Heat Pump Water Heaters* (IEA HPT Annex 46) [17, 18]
* **Table / Section / Page**: Section 2.3.5 (Switzerland), Table 1, Page 54 [17, 18]
* **Year of Data**: 2015 (citing standard SIA 385/2) [17, 18]
* **Values**:
  1. **Single-Family House / Condominium** (*EFH*):
     * **Simple standard**: **40 litres/person/day** (average) / **50 litres/person/day** (maximum) [19]
     * **Normal standard**: **45 litres/person/day** (average) / **60 litres/person/day** (maximum) [19]
     * **High standard**: **55 litres/person/day** (average) / **70 litres/person/day** (maximum) [19]
  2. **Multiple-Family Building** (*MFH*):
     * **Simple standard**: **35 litres/person/day** (average) / **45 litres/person/day** (maximum) [19]
     * **High standard**: **45 litres/person/day** (average) / **60 litres/person/day** (maximum) [19]
  *(Note: The delivery temperature for SIA 385/2 standard liters is **not in the sources** in Table 1, which states only "standard liter per day")* [18].

#### **B. Measured Field Consumption Studies**
* **Multi-Family Houses (Vetsch et al. 2012)**:
  * **Volume Demand**: **36 to 44 litres/person/day** [19]
  * **Temperature**: Storage tank outlet temperatures **> 55 °C** [20]
  * **Source Title**: *Task 1 - Test procedures and Quality Labels for Heat Pump Water Heaters* (IEA HPT Annex 46) [19, 20]
  * **Table / Section / Page**: Section 2.3.5 (Switzerland), Table 2 & text, Pages 54–55 [19, 20]
  * **Building Type**: Multi-family buildings (3 objects, 48 to 73 apartments) [20]
  * **Year of Data**: 2012 [19, 20]

* **Single-Family Houses and Apartments (Heim et al. 2016)**:
  * **Volume Demand**: Mean **40 litres/person/day** (ranging across individual households from **8 to 65 litres/person/day**) [21, 22]
  * **Temperature**: Supplied by electric water heaters at an average supply temperature of **63.9 °C** [22]
  * **Source Title**: *Task 1 - Test procedures and Quality Labels for Heat Pump Water Heaters* (IEA HPT Annex 46) [21]
  * **Table / Section / Page**: Section 2.3.5 (Switzerland), Table 3 & text, Page 55 [21]
  * **Building Type**: Single-family houses and apartments (10 households, Minergie-P standard) [21, 23]
  * **Year of Data**: 2016 [21]

* **Swiss National Field Benchmark (FAWA 2004)**:
  * **Thermal Energy Demand**: **3,811 kWh/year** for a 4-person Single-Family House (**EFH**), corresponding to **952.8 kWh/person/year** or **2.61 kWh/person/day**.
  * **Source Title**: *FAWA – Feldanalyse von Wärmepumpen-Anlagen* (BFE / FWS)
  * **Table / Section / Page**: Table 3, Page 44 & Table 4, Page 55
  * **Building Type**: Single-family house (**EFH**, 4 residents)
  * **Year of Data**: 2004

---

Switzerland For designing domestic hot water systems, the building industry is following the standards SIA 385/1[28] and SIA 385/2 [29]from the Swiss Society of Engineers and Architects (SIA). Major topics are legionella prevention, reduced heat losses of tubes and storage tank, hot water demand, tapping time, and heat tracing.SIA 385/1 defines the basic requirements for domestic hot water systems. SIA 385/2 describes the calculation methods for the planning of domestic hot water systems. Requirements for legionella prevention, heat losses (of tubes and

storage tank), domestic hot water demand, tapping time, and heat tracing, etc. are defined. Table 1 defines the hot water demand requirements in different types of buildings (e.g. single and multiple family houses, simple, normal and high standard)and the recommended tapping profiles for dimensioning of domestic hot water systems [29].
